extraction.name: TravelPlanner
extraction.description: TravelPlanner is a planning benchmark focused on travel planning that provides a rich sandbox environment with nearly four million data records accessible via six tools, along with 1,225 meticulously curated planning intents and reference plans. It evaluates whether language agents can handle complex multi-constraint planning tasks involving flights, accommodations, restaurants, and attractions.
extraction.creator: Jian Xie, Kai Zhang, Jiangjie Chen, Tinghui Zhu, Renze Lou, Yuandong Tian, Yanghua Xiao, Yu Su
extraction.publisher: Fudan University, The Ohio State University, The Pennsylvania State University, Meta AI
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Data was crawled from the Internet to create a static sandbox environment with approximately four million data entries accessible via six tools (CitySearch, FlightSearch, DistanceMatrix, RestaurantSearch, AttractionSearch, AccommodationSearch). Queries were constructed by randomly selecting departure city, destination, and date range, then adjusted for travel duration and hard constraints. Natural language queries were generated using GPT-4. Human annotators (20 graduate students) meticulously annotated reference plans for each query.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Approximately four million data entries crawled from the Internet, organized into six databases: CitySearch (312 entries), FlightSearch (3,827,361 entries), DistanceMatrix (17,603 entries), RestaurantSearch (9,552 entries), AttractionSearch (5,303 entries), and AccommodationSearch (5,064 entries).
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: 20 graduate students were invited to annotate plans for synthesized queries. A plan is deemed eligible only if it meets all constraints outlined in the evaluation script. Authors performed detailed review of every query and plan, rectifying errors. Budget was re-calibrated using costs from human-annotated plans. Multiple stages of human verification were conducted.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Through multiple stages of human verification, the authors ensured high quality of each query and the presence of at least one feasible solution. Budget re-calibration was performed using costs from human-annotated plans to replace heuristic-generated budgets.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: At least one annotated plan per query (eligible plans must meet all constraints)
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-4 was used to generate natural language queries from structured elements; GPT-4-Turbo was used to extract key components from plans for evaluation.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The commonsense evaluation criteria are based on the authors' consensus, which may not reflect universal definitions of commonsense.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Some data is derived from publicly available internet sources and does not represent the authors' viewpoints. Commonsense evaluation criteria are based on authors' consensus and may not be universally applicable.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: TravelPlanner aims to provide an effective benchmark for complex planning research, with evaluation scripts released to foster innovation and aid development of new methods.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking complex planning for LLM-based agents; training using evaluation feedback (e.g., reinforcement learning); testing and validation with strict prohibitions against cheating to maintain fairness.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Evaluation scripts will be released; no explicit versioning or deprecation policy mentioned.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Queries are divided into difficulty levels (Easy, Medium, Hard) based on duration (3, 5, or 7 days) and number of hard constraints; budgets are re-calibrated using costs from human-annotated plans to replace heuristic-generated budgets and reduce the number of feasible plans; dataset is split into training (45 pairs), validation (180), and test (1,000) sets.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Around four million data entries were crawled from the Internet and stored in a static, closed sandbox environment accessible via six tools. Natural language queries were generated using GPT-4 from structured elements (departure city, destination, date range, duration, constraints). Human annotators (20 graduate students) meticulously annotated reference plans, which were validated against evaluation scripts. Authors reviewed every query and plan to rectify errors.
